Head Constable Mukesh Kumar of Maharajpur Outpost under Link Road Police Station in Ghaziabad demanded monthly extortion bribes of Rs 500 from each three-wheeler tempo owner operating between Maharajpur and Sahibabad Mandi under threat of stopping their vehicles. Complainant Mahesh Chand Gupta approached the Vigilance Department at Meerut, and following an inquiry, an anti-corruption trap was executed on 7 September 2000. The respondent was caught red-handed inside his room at the outpost accepting Rs 7,000 in tainted currency collected from fourteen vehicle owners along with a written list, and chemical tests on his hands and pocket yielded positive results. Although the Special Judge (Anti-Corruption), Meerut, acquitted the respondent in May 2003 on unfounded allegations of enmity, the Allahabad High Court reversed the acquittal, found the demand, acceptance, and recovery conclusively established, and convicted him under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with 13(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, sentencing him to one year of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs 3,000. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] vs State of U.P. and connected appeals (Dalbir Singh vs State)
record.summary: The judgment of the Delhi High Court records the following account. On 1 September 2006 Noida police in civil dress took 26-year-old Sonu @ Somveer from his house without justification to Chowki Nithari in connection with a robbery case; he died in the PS Sector-20 lock-up and police claimed suicide by hanging. The trial, transferred to Delhi by the Supreme Court, ended in March 2019 with the conviction of six UP policemen: the Inspector got 3 years RI under Section 365/34 IPC, and two Sub-Inspectors and three constables got 10 years RI under Section 304/34 plus sentences under Sections 220, 365 and 167 IPC, concurrent. The Delhi High Court rejected the suicide theory, held the shirt-noose and GD entries inconclusive or manipulated, and applied the Section 106 Evidence Act presumption on facts within the special knowledge of the police. It dismissed all convict appeals and the complainant's plea for Section 302 enhancement, also upholding the acquittal of SI [name withheld] Pandey. Subcategory corrected from enforced_disappearance to custodial_death as the gravamen is death in custody with 10-year s.304 sentences; the s.365 abduction convictions are retained in the sections. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: Head Constable 41 [name withheld] and Others vs State of Uttarakhand
record.summary: The Uttarakhand High Court affirmed the conviction of Head Constable [name withheld] and other escort personnel under Section 223 of the Indian Penal Code for negligently suffering the escape of an undertrial prisoner from custody. The police party was escorting prisoner Gulzar Khan by train from Haldwani to Dehradun on 12 August 2005 when the personnel fell asleep and the handcuffed prisoner escaped. The trial court had sentenced each appellant to three months' simple imprisonment and a fine of Rs 500. While upholding the conviction, the High Court released the appellants on probation of good conduct for one year under Section 4 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958, and directed refund of the fine. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] v. CBI (Ranbir Singh fake encounter case)
record.case_no: CRL.A. Nos. 1003/2014 and connected appeals (against Special CBI Court, Delhi; trial transferred from Dehradun)
record.summary: The Delhi High Court confirmed the life sentences (plus Rs 50,000 fine each) of seven Uttarakhand policemen for abducting 20-year-old Ranbir Singh after a noon scuffle on 3 July 2009 and shooting him dead in a staged encounter near Raipur, Dehradun. Holding the police self-defence version disproved, the Court confirmed the convictions under Sections 120-B, 302 and 364 read with 120-B IPC, while acquitting A-8 to [name withheld] for want of evidence of the larger plan. The Court cancelled the bail of A-1 to A-7, directing surrender forthwith. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: Constable [name withheld] vs State of Uttarakhand
record.summary: The judgment of the Uttarakhand High Court records the following account. On 25 July 2003 Constable [name withheld] and fellow constables were escorting accused Vishwas Pandit back after production before the Special Judge (Gangster Act) when he escaped from their custody at the railway station. The trial court convicted [name withheld] under Section 223 IPC in August 2018 with a Rs 2,000 fine, acquitting him under Section 224, and the I Additional Sessions Judge, Haridwar dismissed his appeal in December 2022. In criminal revision the Uttarakhand High Court left the findings of the courts below untouched but, noting 20-year pendency, a clean record and probation granted to two co-accused, altered the sentence to release on probation of good conduct for six months on a Rs 30,000 bond. The court directed that Section 12 of the Probation of Offenders Act, 1958 shall apply. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] v. State of Uttarakhand
record.summary: The judgment of the Supreme Court of India records the following account. On the night of 15 November 2004, acting on a liquor-smuggling tip, Head Constable [name withheld] with three constables intercepted a Maruti car near IDPL Gate, Rishikesh, and when it failed to stop, [name withheld] fired a single.38-bore shot that struck front-seat passenger Manisha in the temple, killing her. The Sessions Judge, Dehradun convicted [name withheld] under s.302/34 IPC and s.27(1) Arms Act with life imprisonment but acquitted the three constables. The Uttarakhand High Court dismissed [name withheld]'s appeals confirming his life sentence, while additionally convicting the three constables in the State's appeal. The Supreme Court (2025 INSC 114) quashed the three constables' conviction for want of common intention but affirmed the trial judgment, leaving [name withheld]'s life conviction intact. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] And Ors. vs Queen-Empress
record.summary: The judgment of the Calcutta High Court records the following account. Police arrested several persons on suspicion of murdering Mussamut Dhuri; two constables openly used violence on the prisoners and illegally detained them beyond the lawful period to obtain confessions which proved false, while Head Constable [name withheld], in charge of the investigation, remained in their constant company. The Sessions Judge convicted all three under Section 330 IPC. The High Court upheld all convictions, holding [name withheld] an accomplice in the assaults and illegal detention, and, acting in revision, enhanced his sentence from four months simple to six months rigorous imprisonment while dismissing the constables' appeals. District and victim identities are not stated in the report (Bengal Presidency).

record.title: [name withheld] vs The State
record.summary: The judgment of the Calcutta High Court records the following account. On 25 April 1954 constable [name withheld], on duty on Ranaghat station platform, accused traveller Baidyanath Kundu of blackmarketing two mats, marched him toward the GRP station, demanded money and took his purse containing Rs. 5. Kundu immediately complained to nearby witnesses, identified the constable on the platform, and lodged the FIR at the GRP station. The Special Court, Nadia convicted the constable under Section 161 IPC and fined him Rs. 100. The court believed the eyewitnesses, held the ingredients of Section 161 proved, rejected the extortion-only argument and the challenge to the Special Court trial, affirmed the conviction and retained the fine. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: The State v. [name withheld] & Ors. (with revision by Sailendra Nath Thakur)
record.case_no: Criminal Appeal u/s 378(1) CrPC with Criminal Revision (vs Addl. Sessions Judge, 3rd Court, Howrah order dated 20.08.1985)
record.summary: The Calcutta High Court allowed the State appeal and complainant revision against the 1985 acquittals and convicted an Inspector, Sub-Inspector and Constable of Golabari PS for beating railway employee Kamal Thakur to death in custody on 26 February 1980. The Court held the assault was made to extort a confession, rejecting the alibi and fall-from-roof defence on eyewitness and medical evidence of ruptured kidney and liver. It sentenced two officers to 7 years RI and one to 5 years RI with fines payable to the complainant, affirming the fourth accused's acquittal. The judgment records the torture as an illegal extra-judicial execution in the lock-up. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] @ Nilu vs State of West Bengal
record.summary: The judgment of the Calcutta High Court records the following account. Around 2 a.m. on 23 September 1992, Special Constable [name withheld] of Phool Bagan Police Station, in plain clothes, twice came to pavement-dweller the complainant's jhupri on CIT Road, then forcibly took her in a police vehicle to the station, confined her in a mezzanine barrack room and raped her until about 4:40 a.m. The trial court sentenced him to life under Section 376 IPC with concurrent six years RI under Section 366 IPC. The Division Bench dismissed his appeal and affirmed the conviction and sentence, while acquitting the two co-appellants under Section 366 IPC for want of proof of participation. Trial reference: Sessions Trial No.1(1) of 1993, Phool Bagan P.S. Case No.108 dated 23.09.1992. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] v. State of West Bengal
record.summary: The judgment of the Calcutta High Court records the following account. Around 0.30 a.m. on 4 September 2003 constable [name withheld], on routine two-wheeler checking duty at Ballykhal on G.T. Road, Uttarpara, blocked the road to stop a yellow Hero Honda motorcycle that had sped past the first picket and fired a shot from his service revolver, killing the rider. The trial court convicted him under Section 302 IPC with life imprisonment plus Rs. 10,000 fine on 18 April 2008. The court held there was no dispute he was on duty and that he fired in good faith in due discharge of duty without intent to kill, so the act fell under Exception 3 to Section 300 IPC. It set aside the murder conviction, convicted him under Section 304 Part II IPC instead, and held the 6 years 10 months already undergone commensurate, ordering release if not required in any other case. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] vs State of Kerala
record.summary: The judgment of the Kerala High Court records the following account. Head Constable [name withheld], Station Writer at Fort Police Station, was trapped by the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau on 10 December 1998 accepting two phenolphthalein-marked Rs 100 notes to release a surety's seized bicycle, watch, pen and wallet; though the complainant turned hostile on the Rs 1,500 demand, trap witnesses, chemical tests and recovery from his shirt pocket proved voluntary acceptance. The Special Court had convicted him under Sections 7 and 13(1)(d) read with Section 13(2) of the PC Act with three-year sentences. The Kerala High Court set aside the Section 7 conviction for want of proof of demand but confirmed the Section 13 criminal-misconduct conviction, reducing the sentence to one year rigorous imprisonment with Rs 10,000 fine. Later proceedings: on 29 January 2015, the Supreme Court of India acquitted [name withheld] of all charges on appeal; the convictions recorded in this judgment therefore do not stand. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: The State of Maharashtra vs [name withheld] and Ors.
record.case_no: Criminal Appeal No. 1084 of 1988 with Criminal Revision Application No. 82 of 1989
record.summary: Arun Pandav, 25, was picked up from his home around midnight on 16.12.1985 by Shahupuri police probing an elopement case and found dead with 19 injuries in the lock-up on 17.12.1985. The Sessions Court acquitted all 11 accused policemen, accepting a heart-failure theory. The court held Arun died of assault in the lock-up, the arrest panchanama and station records were fabricated, and convicted accused Nos.1-3 under ss.302/342/218/193 r/w s.34 IPC with concurrent life terms, upholding the acquittal of the other eight. Later proceedings: on 19 November 2013, the Supreme Court of India set aside the order recorded in this judgment (concerning [name withheld], [name withheld]); the outcome recorded here therefore does not stand. Matters not addressed in the cited judgment text are not recorded here.

record.title: [name withheld] and Anr. vs State of Rajasthan
record.summary: The Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court upheld the conviction and life imprisonment of SHO [name withheld] and Constables [name withheld], [name withheld], and [name withheld] of Gangdhar Police Station for the custodial death of Radhey Shyam Darji. The deceased had been illegally detained for interrogation on 5 May 1999 and was tortured to death in police custody on the night of 6-7 May 1999, after which the police personnel transported the body in a police vehicle and burned it to destroy evidence. Affirming the judgment of the Special Judge, SC/ST Court, Jhalawar, the High Court held that the prosecution had conclusively established an unbroken chain of circumstantial evidence proving the offences under Sections 302, 331, 348, and 201 read with Section 34 IPC. Later proceedings: on 27 April 2016, the Supreme Court of India acquitted [name withheld], [name withheld], [name withheld], [name withheld] of all charges on appeal; the convictions recorded in this judgment therefore do not stand. record.unit: Police Station Majhgawan, District Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh Police
record.summary: The Special Judge (PC Act), Jabalpur, on 12 November 2003 convicted Constable Munnalal Rajak of PS Majhgawan for demanding Rs 2,000 from agriculturist Rooplal Patel to let him off an inquiry (threatening jail if unpaid by 7 June 2001), caught in a Lokayukta trap; he drew 1 year RI under s.7 and 2 years RI under s.13(1)(d)/13(2). The MP High Court (Jabalpur, Cr.A. 1976/2003, January 2011) partly allowed the appeal: convictions and fines affirmed, but the s.13 custodial term reduced from 2 years to the 1-year statutory minimum.
record.trial_court_name: Special Judge (Prevention of Corruption Act), Jabalpur

record.title: State (Lokayukt) v. Rajkumar Jaiswal
record.unit: Scheduled Caste Welfare Cell, Damoh, Madhya Pradesh Police
record.summary: The Special Judge, Damoh, on 16 October 2007 convicted DySP Rajkumar Jaiswal of the SC Welfare Cell for demanding a Rs 1 lakh bribe from Dr. Peetamber Budhwani, threatening to implicate him in a sex-scandal/gang-rape case (crime 240/2003) he was investigating, sentencing him under PC Act ss.7 and 13(1)(d)(ii)/13(2) and IPC ss.420 and 388. On 2 May 2017 a Division Bench of the MP High Court (Jabalpur, Cr.A. 2276/2007) affirmed the conviction and directed him to surrender to serve the remaining sentence.
record.trial_court_name: Special Judge, Damoh

record.title: State of Maharashtra v. [name withheld]
record.court: Special Court under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947
record.case_no: Criminal Appeal No.127/1977 (Supreme Court); Bombay HC acquittal 22/23-01-1976
record.summary: Per the Supreme Court judgment of 27-10-1983, Narsingrao Pimple, then a Sub-Inspector attached to Ambarnath Police Station, held up a prohibition charge-sheet against complainant Pandharinath Rege and demanded Rs.2,000 on 09-04-1972 and again on 13-04-1972 to shelve the case, accepting twenty Rs.100 notes in a trap near the Ambarnath octroi naka on 14-04-1972. The trial court convicted him (2 years RI + Rs.2,000 fine) and the Bombay High Court acquitted him in January 1976, but the Supreme Court (Fazal Ali, J.) held the trap proved and the defence a smokescreen, allowing the [name withheld] appeal and convicting him under s.161 IPC and ss.5(1)(a)/5(2) of the 1947 Act with 6 months concurrent RI and Rs.2,000 fine.
record.trial_court_name: Special Court under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 (court name, case number and conviction date not stated in SC judgment; Ambarnath case)

The Additional Sessions Judge, Nagpur convicted him u/s 376 IPC (5 years RI + Rs.1,000 fine, acquitting u/s 342); the Bombay High Court (Nagpur Bench) set the conviction aside, and the Supreme Court allowed the [name withheld] appeal, restoring the trial-court conviction and sentence.

Bhosale), in Sessions Case SC 309/2014, on Saturday 30 January 2016 convicted four Vanrai (Goregaon) police constables — Chandrakant Kamble, Kiran Pingle, Umesh Gosavi and one more — for torturing 20-year-old theft suspect Aniket Khicchi to death in custody on the night of 26 October 2013 (56 injuries; post-mortem: head injury with multiple injuries), sentencing each to 7 years RI plus Rs.10,000 fine under IPC ss.304-II and 330; the first custodial-death conviction in Maharashtra, secured after appointment of special PP Rati Amrolia. record.title: State (Cr. No. 333/1993, Odiansalai PS) v. Police personnel & Anr
record.court: Court of II Additional Sessions Judge, Puducherry
record.summary: The Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Pondicherry (SC No. 11/1995, Cr. No. 333/1993 Odiansalai PS) on 24 June 2002 convicted six Puducherry policemen and a government doctor for the custodial beating to death of Alaker Sekar @ Chandrasekar, brought to Odiansalai police station for interrogation on 29 December 1993, manhandled and brutally injured by the police accused and declared dead at hospital; the prosecution case turned on discrepancies between the first post-mortem (shock due to haemorrhage from cirrhotic varices, only two injuries noted) and a second autopsy (shock from multiple blunt-instrument injuries). Three policemen received seven years RI each and three policemen plus the doctor one year RI each; one policeman died during trial and three were acquitted. The Madras High Court (Justice M.V. Muralidaran, common judgment 29 October 2018 in Crl.A. No. 1051 of 2002 batch) upheld the convictions, and the Supreme Court (Justice Nagarathna, Crl.A. No. 17 of 2019, 17 September 2025) kept the doctor's conviction while modifying his sentence to a fine. Officer names, ranks and exact sections need the HC judgment or trial records.

record.summary: Constable Kishore Singh, ASI Sumer Dan and SHO Sohan Singh kept [name withheld] in a Barmer police lock-up from 2 to 5 February 1994 without producing him before a magistrate and subjected him to third-degree torture culminating in Kishore Singh severing his penis with a razor while Sumer Dan held him; the trial court convicted all three on 21 December 2005 (life for Kishore Singh under s.326, 10 years for Sumer Dan, short terms for Sohan Singh) on a CBI charge-sheet. Thakur & Markandey Katju, JJ., (2011)6SCC369) on 25 October 2010 set aside the HC judgment as a 'gross travesty of justice', sentencing Kishore Singh to 5 years' RI (s.326) + 6 months (s.342), Sumer Dan to 3 years' RI (s.326/120B) + 6 months (s.342), and Sohan Singh to 6 months' SI (s.342), with fines payable as victim compensation.

record.title: State (CBCID) v. [name withheld] & Ors (N. custodial murder and P. gang-rape)
record.summary: The Principal Sessions Judge, Cuddalore (Sessions Case No. 99 of 1993, CBCID Crime Nos. 160-162/1992) on 4 September 1997 convicted two sub-inspectors, a head constable and three constables who, as a special theft-detection team, wrongfully confined [name withheld] at Annamalainagar police station from 30 May to 2 June 1992 on suspicion of theft and beat him to death with lathis and boots, while gang-raping his wife [name withheld] inside the station and beating other detained witnesses. The court sentenced the four rapist-constables to 10 years RI each under section 376(2) IPC plus 3-year terms under sections 348, 330 and 354, and the two sub-inspectors to 3 years RI each (sections 218, 323, 348; A-2 also section 220), remarkably without any murder charge being framed. The Madras High Court confirmed the convictions on 28 November 2002 and the Supreme Court (Mehboob Batcha v. [name withheld], 29 March 2011) dismissed the appeal, lamenting that custodial murder by policemen deserved the death penalty.
record.trial_court_name: Principal Sessions Judge, Cuddalore (Sessions Case No. 99 of 1993)

record.summary: The Principal District and Sessions Judge, Madurai, sitting as the Human Rights Court (CC No. 6/2004), convicted Inspector [name withheld] of Samayanallur police station for illegally detaining S. Anand from 17 April 2003 — shuttling him between Kadupatti and Sholavandan stations without letting his family see him — and brutally beating him with a lathi all over his body, fracturing bones, while also seizing his mother and minor sister at 2 am on 21 April 2003. The court found he violated the victim's fundamental and human rights and sentenced him to a Rs 4,000 fine (Rs 3,500 compensation to the victim) under section 324 IPC read with section 30 of the Human Rights Act, in default one year's RI. The Madras High Court (2 July 2012, S. Anand v. [name withheld]) relied on this conviction while noting the officer had since been promoted [name withheld] despite it.

A-1 and A-2 received life terms for murder. The Madras High Court (Justices R. Balasubramanian and A.C. Arumugaperumal Adityan, Crl.A. Nos. 735, 738 of 2004, 4 December 2006) confirmed the murder, confinement, hurt and evidence convictions of A-1 and A-2 (converting 302/120-B/34 to 302/34 and 324 to 323, sentences maintained), while acquitting A-3 of sections 331/326/354 (convicting him under section 323 with admonition under the Probation of Offenders Act) and dismissing the [name withheld] appeal against A-6's acquittal.

record.title: G. Kandhasamy v. [name withheld]
record.summary: The Krishnagiri CJM on 14 August 2009 convicted Head Constable G. Kandhasamy of Bargur police station for demanding and accepting Rs.2,000 from tempo driver Paranthamanan to release him on bail without remand in a 31 August 2006 motor-accident case (Cr.No.469/2006) and to send his vehicle for MVI inspection promptly, sentencing him to 2 years RI with fine on each count under PC Act ss.7 and 13(2) r/w 13(1)(d). The Madras High Court (Justice G. Jayachandran) on 19 February 2018 dismissed his appeal (Crl.A.No.504 of 2009), holding demand and acceptance proved beyond doubt, confirmed the conviction and sentence, and ordered him secured for the remaining term.
record.trial_court_name: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Krishnagiri (Special Court)

record.title: State v. [name withheld]
record.unit: Prohibition Enforcement Wing, Thiruverumbur Unit, Tiruchirappalli District
record.summary: The CJM/Special Judge, Tiruchirappalli on 29 November 2007 convicted Head Constable [name withheld] of the Prohibition Enforcement Wing, Thiruverumbur Unit, for demanding a monthly mamool of Rs.1,000 from reformed brewer Periyasamy under threat of foisting a prohibition case (including booking him as an absconding accused in Cr.No.2243/2000) and accepting Rs.1,000 in a 10 December 2000 V&AC trap at his house, sentencing him to 1 year RI with fine on each count under PC Act ss.7 and 13(1)(d) r/w 13(2). The Madras High Court (Madurai Bench, Justice G. Jayachandran) on 5 September 2018 dismissed his appeal (Crl.A(MD)No.660/2007), holding demand, acceptance and recovery proved beyond doubt, confirmed the conviction and sentence, and ordered him committed to prison.
record.trial_court_name: Chief Judicial Magistrate/Special Judge, Tiruchirappalli

record.title: State v. [name withheld] (SPE/CBI/ACB/Chennai)
record.unit: Railway Protection Force, Milavittan Out Post, Tuticorin
record.summary: The Special Judge for CBI Cases, Madurai on 18 April 2009 convicted RPF Assistant Sub-Inspector [name withheld], in charge of Milavittan Out Post, Tuticorin, for demanding Rs.2,500 from scrap merchant Paramasivam to not foist a false railway-property theft case against him and accepting it in a 14 March 2007 CBI trap at the Tirunelveli-Madurai bypass signal, sentencing him to 3 years RI with fine on each count under PC Act ss.7 and 13(2) r/w 13(1)(d) concurrently. The Madras High Court (Madurai Bench, Justice G. Jayachandran) on 23 October 2018 dismissed his appeal (Crl.A(MD)No.109/2009), holding the independent witness, co-staff evidence and tainted-money recovery overwhelming, confirmed the conviction and sentence, and ordered him committed to prison.
record.trial_court_name: Special Judge for CBI Cases, Madurai

record.title: State v. [name withheld] (CBI/ACB/Chennai)
record.unit: Delhi Police, IGI Airport Police Station, New Delhi (offence committed at Melur/Madurai during investigation visit)
record.summary: The Special Judge for CBI Cases, Madurai on 26 March 2008 convicted Delhi Police Sub-Inspector [name withheld] (A1) of IGI Airport police station for demanding a Rs.2-lakh bribe (bargained to Rs.50,000) from Melur manpower agent [name withheld] under threat of arrest while camping at Madurai in February 2005 to probe a fake Malaysian visa racket (Cr.No.115/2005 IGI Airport PS), catching him in a CBI trap with phenolphthalein-positive hands, and sentenced him to 2 years RI with fine on each count under PC Act ss.7 and 13(1)(d) r/w 13(2), while acquitting co-accused PC Sibin T. record.trial_court_name: Special Judge for CBI Cases, Madurai

record.title: State (CBI, RC3(S)/2004/CBI/SCB/Chennai) v. Maruthupandiyan & Ors — Kannagi-Murugesan honour killing (2003)
record.court: Special Court for Exclusive Trial of SC/ST (PoA) Act Cases, Cuddalore
record.summary: The Cuddalore Special Court for SC/ST (PoA) Act cases on 24 September 2021 convicted Sub-Inspector K.P. Tamilmaran and Inspector M. Sellamuthu under IPC sections 217/218 and the SC/ST Act for deliberately refusing to register the FIR and fabricating evidence to shield the killers of inter-[name withheld] couple Kannagi and Murugesan, murdered in July 2003, sentencing both officers to life imprisonment. The court found they violated CrPC sections 154/157 and the Police Act to fulfil a [name withheld]-driven design. The Madras High Court confirmed the verdict in June 2022 (reducing only Tamilmaran's sentence to two years) and the Supreme Court upheld the convictions on 28 April 2025 (2025 INSC 576).

record.case_no: Sessions Trial No. 50/2005 (Case Crime No. 455/2004, PS Rishikesh)
record.summary: The Sessions Judge, Dehradun (S.T. No. 50/2005) convicted Head Constable [name withheld] of PS Rishikesh on 06.09.2006 for the 15.11.2004 shooting of woman co-passenger Manisha during a vehicle interception near the IDPL Gate on suspicion of liquor smuggling (Case Crime No. 455/2004), sentencing him to life imprisonment under s.302 r/w s.34 IPC and s.27(1) of the Arms Act while acquitting three constables. The Uttarakhand High Court at Nainital confirmed the conviction on 27.12.2012 (Crl. Appeals 217-218/2006); the convict's Supreme Court appeal abated on his death (2025 INSC 114, decided 28.01.2025), leaving the High Court confirmation standing.
record.trial_court_name: Sessions Judge, Dehradun

record.title: CBI v. [name withheld] & Ors (Karanpur rooftop firing)
record.court: Special Judge for CBI Cases, Dehradun
record.case_no: FIR No. 298-A/94, PS Dalanwala (CBI registered 25.01.1995 on Allahabad HC CWP No. 32982/94; chargesheet 06.04.1996)
record.summary: The Special Judge for CBI Cases at Dehradun on 8 June 2012 convicted four then-constables — [name withheld], [name withheld], [name withheld] and [name withheld] — and sentenced each to seven years' rigorous imprisonment for opening fire from a politician's Karanpur rooftop on unarmed Uttarakhand-statehood agitators on 3 October 1994, killing Rajesh Rawat and grievously injuring Rajiv Mohan and Ravinder Rawat, then cleaning their firearms with hot water and replacing fired cartridges to destroy evidence. The CBI had registered the case on 25 January 1995 on Allahabad High Court orders and chargesheeted the four plus the politician on 6 April 1996; the politician was acquitted.
record.trial_court_name: Special Judge for CBI Cases, Dehradun

record.title: State of Uttarakhand vs Constable [name withheld] (escape of accused Vishal Pandit from escort, 25-07-2003)
record.unit: Uttarakhand Police (escort party; Probation Officer report from Tehri Garhwal)
record.summary: Per the Uttarakhand High Court revision judgment, Constable [name withheld] was convicted under IPC s.223 by the trial court (Criminal Case No. 8747 of 2018, judgment 02-08-2018) for negligently allowing accused Vishwas Pandit to escape from police custody at the railway station on 25-07-2003 while being escorted back after production before the Special Judge (Gangster Act), and was fined Rs 2,000 (acquitted of s.224). His appeal was dismissed by the Ist Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar on 03-12-2022; on revision the High Court on 23-08-2023 released him on six months' probation of good conduct with s.12 of the Probation of Offenders Act to apply. Exact magistrate-court designation of the trial court is not stated in the appellate record.
record.trial_court_name: Trial Court (Magistrate), Haridwar jurisdiction — Criminal Case No. 8747 of 2018 (exact magistrate designation not stated in appellate record; appeal lay before the Ist Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar)

record.title: State v. Constable [name withheld] (Criminal Case No. 8747 of 2018)
record.unit: Uttarakhand Police (escort party producing undertrial before Special Judge (Gangster Act))
record.summary: The Uttarakhand High Court records that Constable [name withheld], whose escort party lost undertrial Vishwas Pandit at the railway station on 25.07.2003 after production before the Special Judge (Gangster Act), was convicted under Section 223 IPC (acquitted under Section 224 IPC) by the Haridwar magistrate court on 02.08.2018 and fined Rs.2,000. The conviction was upheld on appeal (03.12.2022); on revision the court kept the findings intact but substituted a six-month probation bond.
record.trial_court_name: Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar (Criminal Case No. 8747 of 2018; appeal lay before Ist Additional District and Sessions Judge, Haridwar)
